prose.summary: The aluminium window frames you plan to export to India qualify for the preferential CEPA duty rate of 0%. By claiming this preference, you can save 10000.00 AED on your shipment compared to the normal (MFN) rate of 10%. Please follow the checklist below to claim this benefit.
prose.classification: Your product, aluminium window frames, is classified under Indian tariff line 76101000 for doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is medium, so you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA agreement, the normal (MFN) duty rate for this product is 10%, and the preferential CEPA rate is 0%. Your estimated saving is 10000.00 AED based on the shipment value of 100000 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and a value addition (VA) of 45%. CTSH means each non-originating input must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the product, and VA is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials, calculated on an FOB basis (the price loaded on board at the UAE port). Your product meets the rule of origin because the final manufacture in the UAE passed, the minimal operations check passed, the CTSH check passed with all 3 non-originating inputs classified outside subheading 761010, and the VA check passed with a build-down of 49.0% against the 45% threshold.

notes.text: The 0% CEPA rate applies to Basic Customs Duty only; other charges such as IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply. However, because the IGST base includes Basic Customs Duty, the lower duty also reduces the IGST amount.
The agreement refers to box 8 for the certificate, but India's origin rules and certificate form use box 9. Since India's form governs entry into the country, you must use box 9 on your certificate.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so the actual duty amounts will differ from the estimate shown.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply. Because the IGST base includes BCD, a lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources, not the official text.
